why: A block [x, x + size - 1] is free exactly when the first obstacle at or after x lies beyond x + size - 1. Keeping obstacles in sorted order turns each check into one binary search (lower_bound), which is the week's binary search on a dynamic sorted set.
hints: You do not need to look at every cell of the block. Which single obstacle decides the answer?
The nearest obstacle at or to the right of x: if it is inside [x, x + size - 1] the answer is 0, otherwise 1.
Keep obstacles in a sorted list (bisect.insort) and use bisect_left(x) for each check. O(log n) per check plus insertion cost; a balanced tree / SortedList makes inserts O(log n) too.
pitfalls: The block covers x through x + size - 1 inclusive, so size = 3 at x = 3 touches 5.
An obstacle exactly at x blocks the block.
Marking every cell in a set is O(size) per check, too slow for large sizes; coordinates can be huge or negative, so no fixed array.
constraints:
• 1 <= operations.length <= 10^5 (not stated in the source)
  • -10^9 <= x <= 10^9 and 1 <= size <= 10^9 (not stated in the source)
  • Each type-1 operation targets a coordinate with no obstacle yet.
